tools.name: check_certificate
tools.description: Connects to a domain on port 443 and reports its TLS certificate: whether it is trusted and matches the name, the issuer, the expiry date and days left, the lifetime, the chain and the TLS version, what each of its server addresses serves (up to 4 IPv4 and 4 IPv6), and, for certificates from Let’s E

tools.name: check_domain_expiry
tools.description: Looks up a domain registration over RDAP at the registry for its TLD: when it expires, the registrar, the statuses (flagging a hold, redemption, pending delete or pending transfer) and the nameservers. Subdomains are looked up by their registered domain (www.example.co.uk becomes example.co.uk).

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_certificate" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Connects to a domain on port 443 and reports its TLS certificate: whether it is trusted and matches the name, the issuer, the expiry date and days left, the lifetime, the chain and the TLS version." → after: "Connects to a domain on port 443 and reports its TLS certificate: whether it is trusted and matches the name, the issuer, the expiry date and days left, the lifetime, the chain and the TLS version, what each of its server addresses serves (up to 4 IPv4 and 4 IPv6), and, for certificates from Let’s E"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
